Mahol
MAY-hol
n. (father of Chalcol, Darda, Heman, and Ethan, the wise men Solomon surpassed)
Hebrew Machol, a dance, or the sound of dancing, from chul, to whirl or to dance; named once, 1 Kings 4:31.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · In the Text · Related

Biblical Definition

Mahol is named once, and only as a father: “For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all nations round about” (1 Kings 4:31). The verse is a measurement. Solomon's wisdom is being weighed, and the weights chosen are the four wisest men the age could produce — and all four are Mahol's sons. Whatever house this was, it was the house that had the reputation for understanding, so that to say Solomon exceeded the sons of Mahol was to say he exceeded the summit of human learning. The gift itself was from God and had been asked for rightly: “And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, and largeness of heart, even as the sand that is on the sea shore” (1 Kings 4:29). Mahol himself did nothing recorded. He is named because of his sons, as Jesse is named for David and Amram for Moses. A man whose name means a dance fathered the four great minds of his generation and is remembered in one clause as their father. The glory of the household went to the sons, and the honour of the verse went to the One who gave Solomon more.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): Mahol, the father of Ethan, Heman, Chalcol, and Darda, the four wise men whom Solomon's wisdom exceeded, named once, 1 Kings 4:31.

expand to see more

Hebrew Machol, a dance, or the sound of dancing.

From chul, to whirl, to turn about, or to dance.

It occurs once in the Authorized Version, 1 Kings 4:31.

He is named only as the father of four renowned wise men.

His sons are the measure against which Solomon's wisdom is weighed.

Key Scripture

1Ki 4:31 — "For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all nations round about."

1Ki 4:29 — "And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, and largeness of heart, even as the sand that is on the sea shore."

1Ki 4:30 — "And Solomon's wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east country, and all the wisdom of Egypt."

1Ki 4:34 — "And there came of all people to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all kings of the earth, which had heard of his wisdom."

Modern Corruption

Wisdom is treated as a human attainment to be ranked; Scripture ranks it only to show that Solomon's came as a gift and was still not enough to keep him.

expand to see more

The modern handling of wisdom is comparative and self-referential: it measures insight against other insight and calls the top of the list enlightenment. First Kings does hold a comparison — Solomon against the sons of Mahol — but only to show the gift's source. God gave it, in answer to a prayer for an understanding heart rather than for riches or long life, and the nations came to hear it. The register of Mahol's four sons exists to mark a ceiling, and then to say that the ceiling was passed by a man who had asked God for the ability to govern.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the wisest man who ever reigned ended in idolatry, which settles whether natural wisdom can keep a soul. “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom” (Psalm 111:10) is the whole of the matter, and Solomon's own later writing is the proof by subtraction. Mahol's sons were the best the age had, Solomon surpassed them, and both together could not do what the fear of God does.
